subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is current-main source evidence enough to close this billing issue, or should maintainers require a fresh Windows provider run that proves `openclaw chat --session <fresh-key>` does not load prior trajectory context?
rationale: The code now has multiple protections, but the reported failure caused real cross-provider spend and the exact current-main runtime path has not been proven in the review evidence.

options.title: Require fresh runtime proof
options.body: Keep this open until a Windows current-main run records startup token counts and confirms fresh sessions do not ingest previous trajectory files.

options.title: Close from source guardrails
options.body: Accept the current transcript classification, reseed caps, and memory filters as sufficient proof that the reported release-era behavior is fixed.

options.title: Track a narrower follow-up
options.body: Close only after opening a focused follow-up for token-budget observability or startup context accounting if maintainers decide the old root cause is gone.

recommendation.title: Require fresh runtime proof
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a Windows current-main run records startup token counts and confirms fresh sessions do not ingest previous trajectory files.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision centers on session-history reseed and fresh-session context boundaries where hclsys introduced the key raw-reseed guardrail.
